emails.name: Welcome: connect your calendar
emails.goal: Get the one first step done: connect a calendar.

subject_options.benefit: No more double bookings, starting now
subject_options.question: Which calendar should we check first?

emails.preview: Connect it once and booked times stop clashing with the rest of your day.
emails.body:
Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }},

Thanks for signing up. Getting set up takes three steps, and the first one does most of the work: connect your calendar.

Once it's connected, we check your existing events before offering any time, so nobody can book you on top of something you already have.

Steps 2 and 3, setting your hours and sharing your booking link, come in the next emails.

cta.to: the calendar settings page in the app

emails.ps: Stuck? Reply to this email and tell us where.

emails.notes: Keep the PS only once replies go to a mailbox someone reads (see the compliance check).

emails.goal: Get availability set so the first booking lands at a good time.

subject_options.question: How many meetings is too many?

emails.preview: Set your working hours, buffers and a cap on meetings per day.

Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }},

Before you share anything, tell us when you're actually free.

Set your working hours, block off weekends, and add buffers before and after meetings so you get a break between them. You can also cap how many meetings people can book per day, week or month.

Do it now and your first booking lands at a time that suits you.

emails.name: Core feature: your booking link
emails.goal: Get the booking link shared once.

subject_options.benefit: Your booking link, ready to share
subject_options.question: Where do people ask you for a meeting?
subject_options.specific: Put your booking link in your email signature

emails.preview: Make it short, then add it where people already ask for your time.
emails.body:
Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }},

Your booking link is how people pick a time without the back-and-forth. Make it short and easy to remember, then put it where people already ask for your time:

- your email signature
- your website, as an embedded booking page
- your social profiles

The next person who asks "when are you free?" gets a link instead of a list of times.

cta.to: the booking link settings in the app

emails.ps: To embed it on your site, copy the embed code from the same page.

compliance_check.check: Postal address in every commercial email
compliance_check.evidence: Address set in the account; 0 of 7 templates print it.
0 of 7 templates contain an unsubscribe link.
Sender name is the brand; sender email is a developer mailbox. Every subject line describes its email.
compliance_check.action: Send from, and reply to, a mailbox someone reads (for example a hello@ or team address on the same domain).

compliance_check.evidence: 18 subject lines and 6 preview lines: 0 with spam-style wording ('free', 'act now', '!!', money claims) and 0 fake 'Re:' or 'Fwd:' subjects. Subjects, previews and bodies: 0 ALL-CAPS words. The drafts are text with one link each and no images, so the text-to-image balance holds.
Recipients opted in to Email List, and the emails are setup help, not promotions.
Email List is single opt-in; where sign-ups live wasn't given.
compliance_check.action: If any sign-ups are in the EU, UK or Canada, switch Email List to double opt-in or keep a record of each consent.
Confirm in Klaviyo that unsubscribes are suppressed at once.

compliance_check.evidence: Domain authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) isn't readable through the API.
compliance_check.action: Check the sending domain is authenticated in Klaviyo before volume grows.

build_steps: In Klaviyo, create a flow with the trigger 'Added to List: Email List'.
Add the 6 emails in order with time delays of 1 day, 2 days, 3 days, 4 days, 4 days between them (email 1 sends at once).
Pick each email's saved template, or paste the copy into Klaviyo's editor with the footer shown.
Set the sender and reply-to to a mailbox someone reads.
Leave the flow in draft, preview every email, send yourself a test from Klaviyo, then set it live.

measurement.per_email: click rate on the setup link, unsubscribe rate and spam complaints; opens are context only
measurement.goal: not measurable in Klaviyo until the app sends the activation events above; until then, clicks on the setup links stand in
measurement.judge_after: 500 delivered per email or 2 weeks, whichever is later
measurement.target: none published: the account has no sending history; set the baseline from the first 2 weeks
measurement.first_test: email 1, subject A (benefit) against subject C (specific step), split 50/50
measurement.winner_rule: the subject with the higher click rate once each side has at least 500 delivered and at least 2 weeks have passed; until both are true, no winner is called and both subjects keep sending

unknowns: Where sign-ups live, so which consent rule applies.
Whether the sending domain is authenticated and how opt-outs are handled: not readable through the API.
Whether the Placed Order metric receives real orders: the metric exists, but its events weren't pulled.
